blocks.text: Isaiah 26:19's promise that the dead will live and arise is often read alongside Isaiah 25-27 and 65-66, where death’s defeat, bodily revival, renewed Jerusalem, transformed longevity, and new-heavens-and-earth imagery also appear. The extent and meaning of this connection remain disputed, but these passages became foundational for later Jewish and Christian hope concerning resurrection and new creation.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It is broadly aligned with the Masoretic tradition, though it contains thousands of spelling and substantive differences; other Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings from Qumran also show that Isaiah was actively copied and interpreted.
